name: Sunrise alarm clock

lead: A sunrise alarm clock (wake-up light) brightens gradually over about 30 minutes before the set wake time, imitating dawn, and may add sound.
It is used to make waking easier and to support a regular schedule. Trials on dawn simulation show better alertness and mood in some groups, though the evidence is small and mixed.

paras: Gradually rising light through closed eyelids reduces sleep depth and promotes arousal and cortisol rise before waking, easing sleep inertia.

It is generally safe, though light before waking can disrupt late sleep for some. The only study cited here is an experimental trial in young adults, and an older-adult study found no effect on alertness. A regular wake time itself is a major part of the benefit.
